provenance.label: SYNTHETIC / DEMO-ONLY
provenance.description: All initiatives, evidence references, dates, owners, and issue drafts are fictional planning material created for a Copilot-for-Product demo.
limitations: No item is a customer promise or production commitment.
Evidence is deliberately small, invented, and contradictory.
Targets are proposed decision aids rather than measured baselines.
Human decision flags must not be resolved automatically.

horizons.label: Now
horizons.definition: Active discovery and preview-hardening work through September 2026; timing is illustrative.

horizons.label: Next
horizons.definition: Gated options for October through December 2026, entered only after explicit evidence and risk review.

horizons.label: Later
horizons.definition: Uncommitted opportunities for 2027 or later; sequence and scope remain open.

initiatives.title: Harden personal Saved Views preview
initiatives.outcome: Frequent feedback triagers can safely reuse and understand a browser-local filter configuration without mistaking it for synced or shared state.

evidenceReferences.summary: A fictional frequent triager repeatedly rebuilds the same filters.
A synthetic participant values explanation and stale-filter recovery.
An occasional reviewer questions whether the feature is relevant.
A fictional duplicate-name ticket exposes an unresolved naming rule.
A stored criterion must not restore access after a role change.
Apply, update, and save-as-new semantics need separation.
Synthetic later-session reuse is directional, not causal.
Invented parse errors make safe recovery a preview requirement.
Named personal views may use a recognizable mental model.
Mutable-schema products suggest warning and recovery patterns.

risks.description: Renamed, removed, or restricted fields could silently change results.
risks.mitigation: Version and validate stored state, explain omissions, and re-check current access on apply.

risks.description: People may expect views to follow them across devices.
risks.mitigation: Repeat clear local-only language at create and manage surfaces.

risks.description: Ambiguous names and accidental creation may create local clutter.
risks.mitigation: Resolve naming policy and keep rename/delete accessible.

humanDecisionFlags.question: Should local view names be unique, repeatable, or automatically disambiguated?
humanDecisionFlags.requiredBy: Before create-flow acceptance criteria are finalized

humanDecisionFlags.question: Should a partly invalid view apply valid criteria or stop for review?
What combination of reliability, accessibility, and reuse evidence is sufficient to reconsider account sync?

successMeasures.criterion: Review directional movement among eligible synthetic preview users; do not use a single threshold as an automatic ship gate.
Create, apply, rename, delete, and recover complete with keyboard and supported screen-reader checks.
Invalid records do not block Feedback and provide an actionable explanation.

issueDraft.title: [Synthetic demo] Harden browser-local Saved Views preview
issueDraft.body:
## Outcome
Make personal Saved Views reliable, understandable, and accessible while keeping them explicitly browser-local.

## Evidence
Review the synthetic references on initiative `init-saved-views-preview`; they include reuse signals and counter-signals about reach, stale state, and sharing.

## Boundaries
No account sync, team sharing, result snapshots, or sensitive telemetry. Human decisions in the roadmap remain open.

## Done when
Core flows meet the approved acceptance boundary, corrupt state is recoverable, current permissions always win, and local-only language is visible.

childWorkItems.title: Version and validate local view records
acceptanceCriteria: Unsupported or corrupt records cannot block the Feedback page.
Stored records exclude result content, access state, names from telemetry, and filter values from telemetry.

childWorkItems.title: Complete create, apply, rename, and delete flows
acceptanceCriteria: Local-only persistence is explained during creation and management.
Active and edited state are distinct without relying on color.

childWorkItems.title: Explain stale and restricted criteria
acceptanceCriteria: Current permissions are evaluated on every apply.
The user can review, update, or delete an invalid view without leaked restricted context.

childWorkItems.title: Validate keyboard, screen-reader, reflow, and status behavior
acceptanceCriteria: Core flows work without pointer input.
Save, apply, and recovery outcomes are programmatically announced.

initiatives.title: Make feedback result provenance legible
initiatives.outcome: Reviewers can understand which filters and omissions shaped a result set, whether or not it came from a saved view.

evidenceReferences.summary: A fictional participant prioritizes explaining why an item appears.
Permission changes create an omission-explanation need.
Generic market patterns suggest stale-filter warnings.

risks.description: Detailed explanations could overwhelm routine review.
risks.mitigation: Test progressive disclosure and concise summaries.

risks.description: An omission explanation could reveal a restricted source or field.
risks.mitigation: Threat-model content and use non-identifying explanations.

humanDecisionFlags.question: Which filter details stay visible and which use progressive disclosure?

successMeasures.criterion: Synthetic research participants can explain the active criteria and whether any were omitted.

issueDraft.title: [Synthetic demo] Prototype feedback filter provenance
issueDraft.body:
## Outcome
Help reviewers understand the filters and safe omissions shaping the current result set.

## Scope
Prototype progressive disclosure, active/edited language, and permission-safe omission messages. Do not expose restricted field or source details.

childWorkItems.title: Draft filter-summary and omission content
acceptanceCriteria: Copy distinguishes active, edited, stale, and restricted states.
Restricted explanations do not identify inaccessible context.

childWorkItems.title: Prototype progressive disclosure across viewports
acceptanceCriteria: Summary remains understandable at 320 CSS px.
Details are keyboard and screen-reader accessible.

initiatives.title: Evaluate account-synced personal views
initiatives.outcome: The team can decide whether cross-device continuity merits durable account storage without conflating it with sharing.

evidenceReferences.summary: One fictional ticket expected a view on another device.
Directional later-session reuse does not establish cross-device need.
Private exploratory configurations remain important.

risks.description: Durable storage creates migration, retention, export, and deletion obligations.
risks.mitigation: Complete architecture, privacy, and lifecycle review before an experiment.

risks.description: Cross-device infrastructure may not address the reason most synthetic users did not create a view.
risks.mitigation: Require qualitative cross-device evidence and a bounded experiment plan.

humanDecisionFlags.question: Has the local preview met the reliability and reuse gate for a sync experiment?
What retention, deletion, export, and migration policy applies to saved configurations?

successMeasures.criterion: A bounded synthetic study demonstrates a meaningful workflow that local storage cannot support.
Privacy, security, retention, deletion, and migration owners explicitly approve the experiment.

issueDraft.title: [Synthetic demo] Evaluate account sync for personal Saved Views
issueDraft.body:
## Decision to make
Determine whether evidence justifies a bounded cross-device personal-view experiment.

## Gate
Do not implement until local reliability, accessibility, privacy, retention, deletion, and migration questions have named owners and explicit approval. This does not include team sharing.

childWorkItems.title: Study cross-device continuity needs
acceptanceCriteria: Research distinguishes cross-session from cross-device reuse.
Counter-signals and non-user workflows are documented.

childWorkItems.title: Define storage and data-lifecycle options
acceptanceCriteria: Options cover migration, export, retention, and deletion.
Security and privacy reviewers record unresolved risks.

childWorkItems.title: Record the sync experiment decision
acceptanceCriteria: Decision cites evidence and rejected alternatives.
No automatic launch follows from a metric threshold.

initiatives.title: Research curated team views and defaults
initiatives.outcome: Cross-functional teams can evaluate a governed shared-view model without exposing restricted context or publishing private scratch work.

evidenceReferences.summary: A fictional participant prefers a small curated set to many personal views.
A counter-signal favors private scratch configurations.
Role changes make permission-safe application essential.
One fictional request describes governed curation rather than open sharing.
Generic patterns distinguish personal, shared, and default visibility.
View proliferation can create administration costs.

risks.description: A shared definition or count could disclose restricted data.
risks.mitigation: Threat-model definitions, metadata, counts, and application behavior before prototyping with realistic roles.

risks.description: Unbounded creation could replace repeated filter work with discovery and governance work.
risks.mitigation: Test curated ownership, archive, and default semantics before open publishing.

humanDecisionFlags.question: Who may create, edit, archive, and designate a workspace default?
humanDecisionFlags.requiredBy: Before a sharing concept is approved

humanDecisionFlags.question: How should a shared view behave when a viewer cannot access a referenced source or field?
Should sharing and setting a default require distinct permissions?

successMeasures.criterion: Synthetic participants can identify owner, editor, viewer, and default responsibilities without prompting.
Zero disclosures across definition, metadata, counts, and results in role-based review.

issueDraft.title: [Synthetic demo] Research governed team views
issueDraft.body:
## Outcome
Test whether curated team views solve coordination needs while preserving private scratch work and current permissions.

## Non-goal
This issue does not authorize implementation or promise sharing. Permission and governance decisions remain human-owned.

childWorkItems.title: Map owner, editor, viewer, and default-view responsibilities
acceptanceCriteria: Role options cover create, update, archive, transfer, and default designation.
Private-to-shared transition is always intentional.

childWorkItems.title: Threat-model shared criteria and metadata
acceptanceCriteria: Review includes names, criteria, result counts, omission messages, and revoked access.
Current viewer access remains authoritative.

childWorkItems.title: Test a governed sharing concept
acceptanceCriteria: Research includes curation and private-work counter-scenarios.
Findings state sample and synthetic limitations.

initiatives.title: Explore view-based feedback digests
initiatives.outcome: The team can assess whether an intentionally subscribed digest helps periodic reviewers without treating every saved view as a notification.

evidenceReferences.summary: A fictional monthly reviewer may need a different workflow than frequent triagers.
Generic products sometimes connect saved searches to alerts, but consent and freshness differ.

risks.description: Saving a view could be mistaken for consent to receive notifications.
risks.mitigation: Require a separate explicit subscription with frequency and unsubscribe controls.

risks.description: Stale criteria could produce misleading or empty digests outside the product context.
risks.mitigation: Define freshness checks and an in-product recovery path before delivery.

humanDecisionFlags.question: Does a digest solve an observed periodic-review problem better than an in-product reminder or history?
What constitutes explicit consent and who controls frequency?

successMeasures.criterion: Multiple observed workflows establish a recurring need before solution testing.
Zero; save and subscribe remain separate explicit actions.

issueDraft.title: [Synthetic demo] Explore opt-in feedback digests
issueDraft.body:
## Question
Would a separately subscribed digest help periodic reviewers, and is it better than in-product history or reminders?

## Guardrails
A saved view is never notification consent. This is an uncommitted research candidate dependent on durable view semantics and delivery review.

childWorkItems.title: Observe periodic feedback review workflows
acceptanceCriteria: Study compares digest, history, reminder, and no-change options.
Evidence limitations and counter-signals are recorded.

childWorkItems.title: Define explicit subscription and unsubscribe model
acceptanceCriteria: Save and subscribe are separate actions.
Frequency, pause, unsubscribe, and stale-view behavior are covered.
